questions.question:
**Direction: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence.**

He has a ______ nature and the rainforest is a ______ of forest found on earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "kind."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires an adjective to describe the nature of the person mentioned.
 
• For the first blank, **"Kind"** is a suitable word to describe a person's nature as it means having a friendly, generous, and considerate attitude. (परोपकारी; मित्रवत और उदार)
 
 
• **Example**: *He is very **kind**__.*
 
 
 
• ​The second part of the sentence mentions a specific type of forest, which is the rainforest.
 
• **"Kind" **means a group whose members all have the same qualities. (समान गुणों वाले व्यक्तियों का समूह; वर्ग)
 __
 
• **Example**: *There are people of all **kinds**__.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

**Correct sentence**: *He has a __**kind**__ nature and the rainforest is a __**kind**__ of forest found on earth.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (type)** is not a suitable word to describe a person's nature and is not related to the second part of the sentence. (समान विशेषताओं वाले व्‍यक्तियों या वस्‍तुओं का समूह (जो अपने से बड़े समूह का भाग हो); प्रकार या क़िस्‍म)
 
• **Option 2 (caring)** is a suitable word to describe a person's nature, but it does not match the context of the second part of the sentence. (दूसरों के प्रति चिंता और प्‍यार दिखानेवाला; परचिंतक)
 
• **Option 4 (rude)** is the opposite of what is required to describe the person's nature and does not match the context of the second part of the sentence. (अशिष्‍ट (किसी के प्रति) (किसी बात पर))

options.text: A well-mannered man with noble behaviour

questions.solution:

• The idiom **"A man of means" **refers to a person who is affluent and has significant financial resources. (एक व्यक्ति जो समृद्ध है और जिसके पास महत्वपूर्ण वित्तीय संसाधन हैं)

 
 
• **Example**: *He is **a man of means**__.*
 
 
 
• The word **"means"** here refers to wealth or financial resources.
 
• The idiom can be used to describe someone who is financially successful, independent, and has the ability to live a comfortable lifestyle without any financial struggles.
 
• The phrase can also be used to describe someone who has inherited wealth or has acquired it through business or investments.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Don’t panic! / We won’t leave you alone in trouble / when you travelling with us.

options.text: We won’t leave you alone in trouble

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"When you travelling with us".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In time clauses with words like **when, after and until,** we often use **present tense forms **to talk about the future:
 
• **For example:**
 
 
• I'll come home **when I finish work.**
 
• You must wait here **until your father comes.**
 
• They are coming **after they have had dinner.**
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct sentence would be: **Don't panic! We won't leave you alone in trouble when you travel with us. **

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **"Don’t panic!"** – This sentence is free from any grammatical mistakes.

 
 
• It's a command or an imperative sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• The subject (you) is understood and does not need to be stated explicitly.
 
 
 
• **"We won’t leave you alone in trouble" – **This sentence is also error-free.
 
 
• The phrase **'We won't' **is a contraction for **'we will not' **which is grammatically correct.
 
• **'Leave' **is a proper base form of the verb to use after **'will not.' **
 
• The rest of the sentence, **'you alone in trouble,' **correctly follows standard English grammar rules.
